government.note: Parliamentary republic with a unicameral 150-seat National Council. The President has been directly elected in two rounds since 1999 (five-year term, renewable once consecutively); before that the National Council elected the president, and the office was filled by acting officials from March 1998 to June 1999. Referendums are valid only if at least 50% of voters take part; only the 2003 EU accession referendum has met that threshold.

offices.note: First directly elected president from 15 June 1999. Between Michal Kováč's term (ended 2 March 1998) and Schuster's inauguration, presidential powers were exercised by acting office-holders (Mečiar and Gašparovič in 1998, Dzurinda and Migaš in 1998-1999).

system.note: Open-list PR; seats allocated by the largest remainder method with the Hagenbach-Bischoff quota. Threshold 5% for single parties, 7% for two- and three-party alliances and 10% for larger alliances (current law). seats_2000 is the result of the September 1998 election; mid-term changes before 1 January 2000 were not checked.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from the September 1998 National Council vote (shares computed from the vote counts): HZDS 27.0% and SNS 9.1% (national conservative), SDK 26.3% (a centre-right alliance, recorded as liberal conservative), SDĽ 14.7% (social democrat), SMK 9.1% (Hungarian minority party, recorded as regionalist), SOP 8.0% (centre-left, recorded as third_way), KSS 2.8% (communist), Union of the Workers of Slovakia 1.3% (left populist), other lists 1.7%.
